title: Amorak: Sound Design
tagline: Sound design for a 90-second horror animation. Built the creature sound from layered animals, designed all environments, and mixed everything in binaural 3D. The hardest part was making spatial audio feel natural—not just technically correct, but believable.

showcase.title: What I Did
showcase.description: The client sent a locked cut with generic temp sound that didn't fit. I had 4 weeks. I built the creature vocals from organic animal layers (lion, elephant, tiger) instead of synths, designed the environment from scratch to feel old and damp, and mixed everything binaurally so it sounds real on headphones.
showcase.list1: Creature vocals: Real animal layers for organic texture
showcase.list2: Spatial mix: Binaural 3D placement for headphones
showcase.list4: Mix: Frequency carving to keep the monster dominant

overview.title: The Story
overview.desc: A man is carving wood when he hears thunder and sees something through the window. He runs to the basement. The beast breaks in, searches the house. The man hides with an axe. When the beast descends the stairs into the basement, a trapdoor slams shut—it's a trap. The film ends with an apple rolling to his feet. He won.

creatures.title: Creature Sound Design
creatures.desc: I layered 4 animal recordings: lion, elephant, tiger, hippo. Pitched them down for weight. The hippo added high-end rasp.

environment.title: Spatial Audio Workflow
environment.desc: I designed the environment to follow the camera. Dripping water is close and unsettling, while distant chains suggest a larger threat. Binaural panning places every sound in a specific spot around the listener's head.

narrative.title: Final Mix Strategy
narrative.desc: The mix prioritizes the creature. Dynamic ducking pushes the environment down whenever the monster screams or the character breathes.

technical.title: Tools & Technology
technical.description: I used Logic Pro for sound design and Reaper for the final spatial mix. The focus was on binaural audio—creating a 3D soundstage that works on standard headphones.

proximity.title: Logic Pro
proximity.desc: Used for creative sound design, layering animal vocals, and processing individual assets.

frequency.title: Reaper
frequency.desc: Used for the final mixdown, automating spatial movements as the camera moves through the scene.

layering.title: Source Material
layering.desc: A mix of high-quality animal libraries (lion, elephant) and custom foley recorded specifically for this project.

captions.beastroar: Creature sound design frequency visualization — low-frequency rumbles (40-200Hz) layered with mid-range growls for presence
captions.basement: Basement environment spatial audio layers — dripping water, creaking wood, and distant echoes create atmospheric depth
captions.creatureview: Binaural spatial mixing setup — creature positioned using Dear VR Pro with distance-based attenuation
captions.chimney: Environmental detail sound design — fireplace crackling, metallic knife impact, and tension-building acoustic textures
captions.character: Character vocal clarity — dynamic ducking and frequency separation for breaths and grunts in dense soundscape

challenge1.title: Creature vs. Environment
challenge1.problem: The creature's low-end roar clashed with the deep basement rumble.
challenge1.sol3: Centered the creature in the mix

challenge2.title: Spatial Consistency
challenge2.problem: Fast editing made spatial audio feel disjointed.

challenge3.title: Vocal Clarity
challenge3.problem: Character breaths got lost in the loud monster sounds.

hero.subtitle: SOUND DESIGN
hero.description: Complete audio post for a 90-second horror teaser. Client wanted visceral and terrifying. Built the creature from scratch, designed all environments, mixed binaurally so it sounds like you're in the basement with them. 4 weeks, solo work.

creature.title: The Beast's Roar
creature.description: I layered lion, elephant, tiger, and hippo roars, then pitched them down. The low rumbles give it physical weight.

environment.title: Basement Atmosphere
environment.description: The basement feels claustrophobic and threatening. Dripping water. Creaking wood. Chains rattling. Rats scurrying. Thunder rumbles outside. Each sound is placed in 3D space so you know exactly where everything is.
